subject: Archaeology
title: The Invention of the Wheel
description: A 60-second lesson on The Invention of the Wheel.

hook.text: The wheel was not invented for chariots. It was invented for pottery — then someone flipped it sideways.

buildup.text: The potter's wheel appeared in Mesopotamia around 3500 BCE. Wheeled carts followed about 300 years later.

discovery.text: The oldest known wheeled vehicle image is on a Sumerian tablet from Uruk — a simple box on solid wooden discs.

twist.text: Spoked wheels did not appear for another 1,500 years. Early wheels were heavy, slow, and only useful on flat ground.

climax.text: Wheeled transport transformed trade, warfare, and agriculture. It remains one of humanity's most important inventions.

punchline.text: It started as a turntable for clay pots. Someone turned it sideways and changed the world.

quiz.question: What was the wheel originally invented for in Mesopotamia?
options: Transporting heavy stones for temple construction
Making pottery — the potter's wheel came before wheeled carts
Grinding grain into flour at early bakeries
